title: New dental training places and emergency clinic funded in Northern Ireland
html:
Irish health minister Robbie Butler has announced funding for six additional dental foundation training places across Northern Ireland and a new emergency dental clinic in Omagh.

Supported by £787,000 of funding, the additional dental foundation training places bring the number available in Northern Ireland from 30 to 36 for 2026/7.

Chief dental officer for Northern Ireland Caroline Lappin said: ‘Investing in dental training is essential to building a strong and sustainable workforce. These additional places will provide newly qualified dentists with valuable clinical experience and encourage them to remain in health service practice.’

A further £525,000 of recurring funding has been approved for an emergency dental clinic at Omagh Primary Care Complex, aiming to address a longstanding gap in out-of-hours care in the western region.

Minister Butler commented: ‘Improving access to dental care means investing in both the services patients need today and the professionals who will deliver care in the future. Where you live should not determine whether you can access emergency dental treatment.’

Do the new dental training places in Northern Ireland go far enough?

The funding for the training places and clinic was first allocated in April. While acknowledging the ‘significant efforts’ of the health minister in securing the £8 million investment, the British Dental Association (BDA) Northern Ireland said it was ultimately ‘insufficient’.

Due to a ‘fundamental mismatch between fees paid by the government, and the true cost of providing modern dental care’, the BDA said an ‘unviable’ funding gap remains.

Ciara Gallagher, chair of the BDA Northern Ireland Dental Practice Committee, stressed that health service dentistry in Northern Ireland was ‘on borrowed time’ and called for greater urgency and ambition.

She continued: ‘Our executive must now go further and faster and focus on the fundamentals. Dentists need to see a future in the NHS and know they won’t lose money treating NHS patients.’

The BDA called for fundamental reform of the dental payment system alongside the pledged funding.
